clue.text: Starts to revitalise crêperie "avec chef nouveau et 'sexy' menu nouveau" — pardonnez-moi!

indicators.note: French for new, so the chef and the letters before it come out in a new arrangement
the starts of the two following words supply only their opening letters
the second French new says the words sexy and menu are likewise remade

explanation.surface: A franglais restaurant review: a pancake house is revived by a new chef and a racy new bill of fare, with apologies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to' gives R and C; both 'nouveau's are anagram signals over CHEF and SEXY MENU, and the French 'avec' (with) and 'et' (and) are link words. All fourteen letters rearrange together.
explanation.definitionFit: The French plea for forgiveness is the English idiom used to apologise for swearing, a joke on using French.

clue.text: Unconventional type manufacturing far better linen

indicators.note: making something new out of raw material, so the letters of the three words are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone eccentric is producing linen of much finer quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufacturing' is the anagram signal over FAR BETTER LINEN, fourteen letters giving the French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase for a shocking child is used for any maverick person who flouts convention.

clue.text: Completely fill military order

definitions.meaning: to load fully, as one does a battery or a glass
a command to rush the enemy, as in a cavalry attack

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both to load something to full capacity and the command for troops to attack.

clue.text: Bright spark that is in work before afternoon

parts.note: SC is short for scilicet, Latin for that is to say
taken as written
to till is to work the soil
A is a dictionary abbreviation for afternoon, as in a timetable

explanation.surface: A clever person is busy at the office before lunchtime is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bright spark' suggests a clever person, but here it is a literal spark or flicker; 'before' is a link placing TILL ahead of A.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is literally a spark, and figuratively a tiny trace of something.

clue.text: Projector's house set between two groups of three

indicators.note: placed in the middle of the two trios, so the house goes inside them

parts.note: the Magi are the three wise men
a tern is a set of three, as in a lottery win on three numbers
a clan, like a noble house, is a family line

explanation.surface: A cinema projector being housed between two trios of objects.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', a link word; 'set between' puts the house inside the two trios, so 'Projector' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An early slide projector that cast painted images onto a screen went by this name.

clue.text: See 1
On for facsimile

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.definitionFit: A repro is a reproduction, a copy of an original such as furniture or a print.

clue.text: Well-seasoned teachers bomb, I'm surprised to have to admit

parts.note: NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British teaching union

indicators.note: to let in, so one piece is placed within the exclamation

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise
egg is old RAF slang for a bomb

explanation.surface: An admission of shock that teachers have failed badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bomb' looks like a verb meaning flop, but it is wartime airmen's slang; 'to have to admit' means the exclamation takes it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is heavily spiced with the brown kernel used in puddings could be described this way.

clue.text: Letters may be appended with it in respect of unpaid amount

definitions.text: Letters may be appended with it

parts.note: an honorary post is held without salary
a degree is an extent or amount, as in to some degree

explanation.surface: A formal note about a sum of money owed that was never paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' are the initials after a name, such as DLitt, which an honoris causa award lets one add; 'in respect of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Universities confer such awards on notable people, who may then put the post-nominal initials after their name.

clue.text: Breaking out in passion over long-legged bird

parts.note: flaming describes someone bursting into a rage
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper about a wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The pink wading bird is famous for its very long thin legs.

clue.text: It's the ticket boy has in pocket

indicators.note: the boy holds the pocket within him

parts.note: a son is a boy
a pot is to pocket a ball in snooker or pool

explanation.surface: A lad has a railway ticket in his pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pocket' is a snooker word: to pot a ball is to pocket it. 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Just the ticket' is an idiom for exactly right, the same as precisely correct.

clue.text: Looking back, awful Torres twisted muscle during international

indicators.note: within the span of, so the other pieces sit inside the abbreviation
used as a signal that the footballer's name is badly mangled
a second signal that the footballer's name is bent out of shape

parts.note: pec is short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: Fernando Torres, a Spanish striker, pulled a muscle playing for his country.
explanation.walkthrough: Fernando Torres is a Spanish footballer; 'awful' and 'twisted' are both anagram signals on his surname, and 'during' places everything inside the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: In retrospect means when viewed with hindsight, reviewing the past.

clue.text: Near the onset of the dark

parts.note: nigh means near

indicators.note: the start of the following word supplies only its first letter

explanation.surface: Approaching the beginning of darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the time of darkness, so the dark stands in for it.

clue.text: Artillery chap, one in food factory taking year off

indicators.note: the number goes within the shortened factory
taking the year off means it is removed from the factory word

parts.note: a cannery is a factory where food is tinned
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gunner who works at a tinning plant takes twelve months off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking year off' strips the year letter from the factory word before 'in' puts the number inside it; 'taking' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannoneer is a soldier who fires cannon, an artilleryman.

clue.text: Nonetheless, Arsenal "Gooner" mutates to Chelsea aficionado

indicators.note: changes form, so the letters of the two football words are rearranged

parts.note: read as none (nought, O) less, so an O is left over from the anagram

explanation.surface: A fan of rival club Arsenal, known as a Gooner, somehow turns into a Chelsea supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal fans are nicknamed Gooners. Chelsea is not the football club but the smart London district; a Sloane Ranger is a posh young person from around Sloane Square.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloane Rangers were the upper-class set associated with the Chelsea area of London, fond of its society life.

clue.text: Unemotional way seen through a quote from down under?

indicators.note: the way passes through the middle of the other letters
in a down clue, read from the bottom upwards, so the word is backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote
a path is a way

explanation.surface: Is a flat, unfeeling remark the sort of thing an Australian would say?
explanation.walkthrough: 'down under' suggests Australia; in a down clue it means CITE written upwards, giving ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathetic means showing no interest or feeling, indifferent.

clue.text: See 1
Scream at swerving vehicle

indicators.note: veering about, so the letters of the two words change course

explanation.surface: Someone yells at a car that is veering about the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam car is a road vehicle driven by a steam engine, like early Stanley models.

clue.text: I used to be ardent about farm machinery, but I'm cooler now

definitions.text: I used to be ardent about farm machinery, but I'm cooler now

parts.words: I used to be ardent about farm machinery, but I'm cooler now
parts.note: a former tractor enthusiast speaks, but split differently the words name an appliance that cools a kitchen

explanation.walkthrough: Read as EX-TRACTOR FAN, a former enthusiast for tractors; 'cooler' is both less keen and a device that cools.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan that draws hot air or steam out of a room cools it, hence a cooler.

clue.text: Following college outside Europe, perhaps, front up for business

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: the continent wraps around the college letter

parts.note: Europe is one example of a continent; Asia is another

explanation.surface: After university the graduate goes abroad and sets up shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Europe, perhaps' is a definition by example: the continent needed here is ASIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascia is the signboard over a shopfront, displayed when a shop is trading.

clue.text: See 8
Slower to progress, maybe reading new word in classic

parts.note: R is reading, one of the three Rs of schooling

indicators.note: the remade word goes within the race name

parts.note: the Oaks is one of the five English classic horse races

indicators.note: made anew, so the letters of the word come out rearranged

explanation.surface: Reading a fresh word in a classic novel slows one down.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oaks is a flat race for fillies run at Epsom; 'new' rearranges the word, and 'in' puts it inside the race name.
explanation.definitionFit: Road repairs hold up traffic, so they are an example of something that slows progress.

clue.text: Cause smoke for the audience

indicators.note: what listeners hear, so the word sounds the same but is spelt differently

parts.note: to reek is to give off smoke, as a chimney does

explanation.surface: Someone lights up in front of the theatre crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreak havoc is to cause it, to inflict damage.

clue.text: Strain to lift what's reversed onto road

indicators.note: turned round, so the exclamation is read backwards

parts.note: eh? is a request to repeat, like what?
Ave is an abbreviation for avenue, a road

explanation.surface: A struggle to raise a car that has been backed out onto the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to haul something heavy upwards with great effort.

clue.text: Argue with bishop and rector about the "Son of God"?

indicators.note: around, so the two abbreviations go either side of the name

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
David Icke, a British broadcaster turned conspiracy theorist, once declared himself a son of God

explanation.surface: A dispute with clergy over a messianic claim.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks hint that it is a self-proclaimed son of God: David Icke, a former BBC sports presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: To bicker is to squabble over petty things.

clue.text: Budget? Divers can't, cutting back

indicators.note: slicing into, so the jumbled letters go inside the other word

parts.note: the rear is the back

indicators.note: means various, so the letters of the word are in assorted order

explanation.surface: Underwater swimmers are unable to manage a cutback on spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' looks like swimmers but is an old word for sundry, giving NTAC from CAN'T, which cuts REAR. Budget is a car-hire company.
explanation.definitionFit: Budget is a well-known car hire firm, an example of a rental company.

clue.text: Victorian battle orders to duke — so take care

indicators.note: arranges, so the letters of the following words are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A general orders a duke to be careful.
explanation.walkthrough: Victorian here means of the Australian state of Victoria: the 1854 gold miners' revolt at Ballarat.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the 1854 armed rebellion of gold miners at Ballarat, Victoria, crushed by colonial troops.
